---
title: "Usage"
---

## Intended New Repository Flow

1. Start a new repository from a `repo-familiar` template.
2. Select project type, agent harnesses, model/provider preferences, advisory profiles, skills, and documentation mode with flags or `questionary` prompts.
3. Generate `.agents/`, `AGENTS.md`, starter skills, and a project plan.
4. Generate a Quarto documentation scaffold for plans, decisions, research, and user stories.
5. Run `grill-with-docs` to challenge the generated plan before implementation begins.

Generated assets should be copied into the downstream repository by default. The generator should also write `.repo-familiar/bootstrap.yml`, recording the `repo-familiar` source and version so future upgrade tooling can reason about what was created.

For command sequencing, ownership boundaries, and targeted add safety, see [Bootstrap Lifecycle](./bootstrap-lifecycle.qmd).

## Current Generator CLI

Run the minimal generator from this checkout:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar generate \
  --name "Demo Project" \
  --description "A generated demo." \
  --output /path/to/demo-project \
  --agent-harness opencode \
  --agent-harness paseo \
  --model-profile default-coding \
  --tool-profile cq \
  --memory-profile memory-local \
  --public-interest-profile public-interest-digital \
  --skill cq \
  --skill session-focus \
  --skill grill-with-docs
```

The generator writes a basic downstream repository with vendored assets, advisory profile files, selected skills, skill source provenance, Quarto docs, and bootstrap metadata.

Use `--interactive` to answer prompts instead of passing every flag:

```bash
uv sync
uv run python -m repo_familiar generate --interactive
```

`questionary` is imported only for interactive commands. `uv sync` installs it from project dependencies.

Use `--dry-run` to preview the generated assets before writing them. The generator refuses to write into a non-empty directory unless `--force` is passed.

To include multiple harnesses or model profiles, repeat the flags:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar generate \
  --name "Demo Project" \
  --output /path/to/demo-project \
  --agent-harness opencode \
  --agent-harness paseo \
  --agent-harness hermes \
  --model-profile default-coding \
  --model-profile budget-review \
  --prompt-profile prompt-migration-gpt55 \
  --repomap-profile hamilton-dag
```

Minimum metadata:

```yaml
schema_version: 2
bootstrap_mode: new_repository
reference_source:
  type: git
  url: https://github.com/<owner>/repo-familiar
  ref: <tag-or-commit>
generated_at: <iso-8601 timestamp>
generator:
  name: repo-familiar
  version: <version-or-commit>
selected_options:
  template: <template-name>
  agent_harnesses: []
  model_profiles: []
  tool_profiles: []
  memory_profiles: []
  prompt_profiles: []
  safety_profiles: []
  privacy_profiles: []
  repomap_profiles: []
  sandbox_profiles: []
  secrets_profiles: []
  design_profiles: []
  worktree_profiles: []
  public_interest_profiles: []
  sops_age_recipients: []
  skills: []
  docs: quarto
generated_assets:
  - path: AGENTS.md
    kind: agent_instructions
    source: templates/basic/AGENTS.md.tmpl
    content_sha256: <sha256>
  - path: .agents/models.yml
    kind: template_config
    source: templates/basic/.agents/models.yml.tmpl
    content_sha256: <sha256>
  - path: .agents/skill-sources.yml
    kind: template_config
    source: templates/basic/.agents/skill-sources.yml.tmpl
    content_sha256: <sha256>
  - path: docs/_quarto.yml
    kind: documentation
    source: templates/basic/docs/_quarto.yml.tmpl
    content_sha256: <sha256>
render_context:
  project_name: <project-name>
  project_description: <project-description>
  template: <template-name>
  docs: quarto
  selected_options_sha256: <sha256>
  source: generation_inputs
managed_surfaces:
  - id: repository-foundation
    version: 1
    template: <template-name>
    state: written
    comparison_basis: content_sha256
    strategy: manual_review
    render_context_sha256: <sha256>
    project_name: <project-name>
    project_description: <project-description>
    docs: quarto
    selected_options_sha256: <sha256>
    render_context_source: generation_inputs
managed_surface_assets:
  - surface_id: repository-foundation
    path: AGENTS.md
    state: written
    comparison_basis: content_sha256
    strategy: manual_review
    content_sha256: <sha256>
history:
  - id: <operation-id>
    at: <iso-8601 timestamp>
    command: generate
    mode: apply
    surface_id: repository-foundation
```

Allowed `kind` values are `agent_instructions`, `skill`, `documentation`, `template_config`, `project_plan`, `metadata`, `dependency_manifest`, `dependency_lock`, `source_code`, `test_code`, and `data_fixture`.

## Model Profiles

Generated projects should use `.agents/models.yml` for model/provider profiles. Bootstrap metadata records selected profile names only:

```yaml
selected_options:
  model_profiles:
    - default-coding
    - budget-review
```

Do not store provider secrets in `.agents/models.yml` or `.repo-familiar/bootstrap.yml`.

Example model profile file:

```yaml
profiles:
  default-coding:
    provider: openai
    model: gpt-5.5
    use: general coding and repository maintenance
    harnesses:
      - opencode
    notes:
      latency: medium
      cost: high
      strengths:
        - codebase editing
        - documentation
```

Profile names should be treated as stable handles for generation choices and future upgrades.

## Existing Repository Setup

Before changing an existing repository, ask for advice and audit the proposed changes:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar advise --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar audit --path /path/to/repo
```

Preview targeted add commands first when you only want one class of defaults:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-memory --path /path/to/repo --memory-profile memory-local
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill cq
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill session-focus
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill grill-with-docs
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill get-api-docs
```

Apply the same selections only after the preview matches the intended additive change:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-memory --path /path/to/repo --memory-profile memory-local --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill cq --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill session-focus --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill grill-with-docs --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill get-api-docs --apply
```

Migrate existing Metadata v1 before attaching an independently implemented capability:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar migrate-metadata --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar migrate-metadata --path /path/to/repo --apply
```

Preview a Managed Surface attachment. Exact matches can be attached metadata-only; differing current files require explicit acceptance and missing files block attachment:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar attach \
  --path /path/to/repo \
  --surface fastapi-api \
  --template static-quarto-application

uv run python -m repo_familiar attach \
  --path /path/to/repo \
  --surface fastapi-api \
  --template static-quarto-application \
  --apply --accept-current
```

For independently implemented layouts, select the current files explicitly:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar attach \
  --path /path/to/repo \
  --surface fastapi-api \
  --template static-quarto-application \
  --asset service/api.py \
  --asset service/test_api.py \
  --apply --accept-current
```

Preview template promotion without writing files or metadata:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar migrate-template \
  --path /path/to/repo \
  --to python-reproducible
```

Use the read-only profile registry ergonomics when you need the built-in summaries or full field details for a profile family:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar catalog model
uv run python -m repo_familiar catalog secrets --format json
uv run python -m repo_familiar describe tool cq
uv run python -m repo_familiar describe public-interest child-rights-digital --format json
```

## Project Plan Inputs

A generated plan should capture:

- Project goals and non-goals.
- Technical preferences and explicit constraints.
- Agent harnesses and `.agents/models.yml` model-provider assumptions.
- Selected skill provenance in `.agents/skill-sources.yml`.
- Documentation expectations.
- Initial milestones and review checkpoints.
